app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

insights: No recent frontend-proxy traces had latency > 9000 ms caused by image-provider; observed high latencies were in the ~9–25s range and attributed to waiting on upstream 'frontend'

Error-only traces for frontend-proxy contained multiple connect ECONNREFUSED to 10.96.54.64:8080 (shipping service), and one large error trace (latency ~760s) referencing shipping POST failure — indicates some downstream services experienced refused connections, but these were separate error cases

Trace c90da868... showed a client-side fetch span (frontend-proxy) with duration 25000 ms; Envoy router egress spans had upstream_cluster=frontend and upstream_address=10.96.18.88:8080 — indicating Envoy/front-end-proxy spent most of the time waiting on the 'frontend' upstream

Trace 45d79d06... (duration ~10.685s) and trace dafa1b35... (~9.336s) both show Envoy/router egress spans with upstream_cluster=frontend and long durations, confirming consistent attribution to 'frontend' upstream rather than image-provider

Spans from frontend, product-catalog, ad, and database show normal durations for their internal operations (e.g., product-catalog ListProducts ~1.2s server span, DB queries ~0.7s) — these do not account for the major Envoy wait time
Envoy spans include fetch/connect lifecycle logs (connectStart, responseStart, responseEnd) showing prolonged connection/response timing on the frontend upstream in long traces

Conclusion: High latency observed at frontend-proxy (Envoy) is caused by blocking/waiting on the upstream service 'frontend' (upstream_address 10.96.18.88:8080). Image-provider is not responsible for these long waits.

final_report.root_cause: Envoy frontend-proxy observed repeated long blocking waits while calling the upstream service 'frontend' (upstream_address=10.96.18.88:8080). Multiple high-latency traces show Envoy/client spans and router egress spans with upstream_cluster=frontend consuming ~9–25s of the request.
